description: Run a script on Linux instances to create symbol table details

AccessKeyId.description: (Required) AccesskeyID to store evidence details in S3.

SecretAccessKey.description: (Required) SecretAccessKey to store evidence details in S3

SessionToken.description: (Required) SessionToken to store evidence details in S3.

runCommand: #!/bin/bash
# Amazon Linux 2 symbol table build. Mirrors the failure contract of its AL2023
# sibling: exits non-zero when no usable ISF was produced, instead of warning
# and exiting 0 while the tools loader reported CREATE_COMPLETE.
# Amazon Linux 2 is end of life and its system Python is 3.7, below the 3.8
# floor volatility3 requires, so prefer an AL2023 builder. This path exists for
# deployments that pin an AL2 builder AMI.
set -o pipefail
fail() { echo "SYMBOL_BUILD_FAILED: $1" >&2; exit 1; }
cd /tmp || fail 'cannot enter /tmp'
sudo rm -rf forensic-profile-builder
mkdir -p forensic-profile-builder || fail 'cannot create the work directory'
cd forensic-profile-builder || fail 'cannot enter the work directory'
sudo yum update -y
sudo yum install git wget -y || fail 'unable to install git and wget'
unamerelease=$(uname -r)
kernel_name=$(uname -s)
kernel_line=$(echo "$unamerelease" | cut -d. -f1,2)
sudo yum groupinstall 'Development Tools' -y
# -y is required: SSM runs this non-interactively, so without it yum reads
# EOF at the confirmation prompt and aborts, leaving no debug vmlinux and
# therefore no symbol table - the original cause of an empty ISF upload.

sudo yum --enablerepo='*debuginfo' install -y "kernel${kernel_line}-debuginfo-${unamerelease}" || sudo yum --enablerepo='*debuginfo' install -y "kernel-debuginfo-${unamerelease}" || fail "no kernel-debuginfo package for ${unamerelease} - Amazon Linux 2 stopped publishing these after end of life"
sudo yum install "kernel-devel-${unamerelease}" -y || sudo yum install "kernel${kernel_line}-devel-${unamerelease}" -y || fail "no kernel-devel package for ${unamerelease}"
# dwarf2json used to be fetched from an individual's repository
# (kevthehermit/volatility_symbols) off the default branch, with no tag, no
# signature and no digest, and then executed. Whoever controlled that branch
# controlled a binary that reads the kernel's debug symbols on the builder.
# It now comes from the volatilityfoundation release the tool actually belongs
# to, pinned by tag and verified by digest before it is made executable. The
# digest was taken from the published asset and cross-checked against the size
# GitHub reports for it (2986584 bytes). Using the release binary rather than
# building from source, as the AL2023 and RHEL8 siblings do, avoids needing a
# Go toolchain on an end-of-life Amazon Linux 2 builder.
DWARF2JSON_VERSION=v0.9.0
DWARF2JSON_SHA256=e2e75ba5bc9c22bc38a48edffbb050456d089d54998d54f46cb580223d9fbc6b
wget -q -O dwarf2json "https://github.com/volatilityfoundation/dwarf2json/releases/download/${DWARF2JSON_VERSION}/dwarf2json-linux-amd64" || fail "cannot download dwarf2json ${DWARF2JSON_VERSION}"
test -s dwarf2json || fail 'the downloaded dwarf2json is empty'
dwarf2json_actual=$(sha256sum dwarf2json | cut -d' ' -f1)
# Refuse to execute it rather than warn: a mismatch means the binary that is
# about to read this kernel's symbols is not the one that was reviewed.
[ "$dwarf2json_actual" = "$DWARF2JSON_SHA256" ] || fail "dwarf2json ${DWARF2JSON_VERSION} failed digest verification - expected ${DWARF2JSON_SHA256}, got ${dwarf2json_actual}"
echo "dwarf2json ${DWARF2JSON_VERSION} verified against its pinned digest"
chmod +x dwarf2json || fail 'cannot make dwarf2json executable'
sudo cp "/boot/System.map-${unamerelease}" . || fail "no System.map for ${unamerelease}"
sudo cp "/usr/lib/debug/lib/modules/${unamerelease}/vmlinux" . || fail "no debug vmlinux for ${unamerelease} - cannot build a symbol table"
test -s vmlinux || fail "the debug vmlinux for ${unamerelease} is empty - cannot build a symbol table"
isf="${kernel_name}-${unamerelease}.json"
# sudo does not affect the redirect, so the ISF was written as the invoking
# user anyway. Take ownership of the inputs instead and run dwarf2json
# unprivileged: it does not need root to read them.
sudo chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" vmlinux "System.map-${unamerelease}" || fail 'cannot take ownership of the debug symbols'
./dwarf2json linux --system-map "System.map-${unamerelease}" --elf vmlinux > "$isf" || fail 'dwarf2json failed'
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID={{AccessKeyId}}
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY={{SecretAccessKey}}
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN={{SessionToken}}
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION={{Region}}
aws configure set default.s3.max_concurrent_requests 20
# Never publish an empty or malformed ISF file: it exists, so downstream
# presence checks accept it and the investigation then yields no rows. Shape is
# not content either - a dwarf2json run that was killed part way through leaves
# a file of about 134 bytes whose maps are all empty. Require populated maps
# plus what volatility3 actually reads: symbols.linux_banner.constant_data,
# which is the only thing automagic can match an ISF to a capture with (see
# framework/automagic/symbol_cache.py), init_task to walk processes, and the
# task_struct definition. The path goes in through argv rather than through the
# program text.

python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); s=d.get("symbols") or {}; b=d.get("base_types") or {}; u=d.get("user_types") or {}; banner=(s.get("linux_banner") or {}).get("constant_data"); sys.exit(0 if (s and b and u and banner and "init_task" in s and "task_struct" in u) else 1)' "/tmp/forensic-profile-builder/$isf" 2>/dev/null || fail "symbol table for ${unamerelease} is empty or not a valid volatility3 ISF"
aws s3 cp "/tmp/forensic-profile-builder/$isf" s3://{{s3bucket}}/volatility3/symbols/ --acl bucket-owner-full-control || fail 's3 upload of the symbol table failed'
echo s3 copy complete
ls -ltr
exit 0;
